newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan aims to raise $2-5 bln from privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan aims to raise $2-5 bln from privatisation.

text.p: Pakistan hopes to raise $2 billion to $5 billion from sales of state assets in calendar 1997, the caretaker government's finance chief said on Wednesday.
"I am expecting privatisation to yield $2 billion to $5 billion this year," Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to the prime minister, told a news conference.
He said he expected Habib Credit and Investment Bank Ltd, now a part of state- owned Habib Bank Ltd, to be sold by the end of February to one of 16 prospective buyers.
Burki said the government was expected to sell its remaining shares in the privatised Allied Bank Ltd and Muslim Commercial Bank in the next couple of months.
Plans were also under way to privatise Pakistan International Airline Corp, and Pakistan State Oil, he added, but gave no timetable.
He gave no deadline for the long-delayed privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd, generally regarded as the jewel among Pakistan's state-owned assets.
Several other state-owned concerns, including electricity companies, power stations, banks, railways, airports and various industrial units are also due to be privatised.

The caretaker government, installed by President Farooq Leghari after sacking Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5, has only a few more days of its assigned three-month term to run. National and provincial elections take place on Monday.
